body.statement:
There are constants \(n_0\in\mathbb N\) and \(C_L<\infty\), depending only on the fixed class constants and \(\eta\), such that the following holds for every \(n\ge n_0\). Choose \((h,k)\) by deterministic minimization of
\[
 B(h,k)+S(h,k,\eta)+G(h,k,\eta,\epsilon_n,\delta_n)
\]
over \(0<h\le r_0\), integers \(k\ge k_{\mathrm{poly}}\), and \(m h^d\ge C_S^2\log(8/\eta)\), with no upper restriction relating \(k\) to \(m h^d\). For any deterministic pilot spline dimensions \(J_\pi,J_\mu\ge1\),
\[
 \sup_{Q\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{att}}}
 \mathbb E_Q[\operatorname{length}\{C_n(h,k)\}]
 \le C_L\{1\wedge r_{\mathrm{up}}\}.
\]
Here \(r_{\mathrm{up}}=r_{\mathrm{np}}\vee r_{\mathrm{reg}}\vee r_{\mathrm{ho}}\) is the untruncated rate in Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}phase\text{-}rate}\), with \(\bar q=\min\{q,\gamma\}\); the achieved length bound is saturated by the displayed factor \(1\wedge r_{\mathrm{up}}\). Thus the length of this global-sensitivity construction is governed by the privacy-free term, the ordinary private-regression term, and a higher-order term which equals the \(q\)-branch for \(q<\gamma\) and the private-Gram branch \(N_{\mathrm{priv}}^{-\gamma/(\gamma+2d)}\) for \(q\ge\gamma\). No matching full-class lower claim or full-class frontier claim is made.
body.justification: On \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{att}}\), the result gives an auditable privacy phase diagram for the saturated achieved length \(1\wedge(r_{\mathrm{np}}\vee r_{\mathrm{reg}}\vee r_{\mathrm{ho}})\); clipping the center preserves the deterministic bound \(2R_n\wedge2\) and every tuning calculation.
body.gap: NiuEtAl2022 gives a private heterogeneous-effect meta-learner and composition analysis but no finite-sample uniformly honest pointwise H\"older CATE expected-length phase.  CaiChakrabortyVuursteen2024 gives a nearby pointwise nonparametric-regression privacy benchmark in a heterogeneous distributed experiment, including a central-private comparison, but not causal nuisance cancellation, this single-curator replacement-private interval, or its attainable-class phase and bracket.
body.consumer: Study designers working in the attainable uniform-design model can select bandwidth, higher-order dimension, and privacy budget to meet a prespecified interval-width requirement with a release that is always an interval.
body.proof_tex:
Put
\[
 x=\log(8/\eta),\qquad M=mh^d,\qquad \ell=hk^{-1/d},
\]
and define
\[
 r_o=n^{-1/(2+d/\gamma)},
 \qquad
 r_2=n^{-1/\{1+d/(2\gamma)+d/(2q)\}}.
\tag{1}
\]
The declared domains give \(d\ge1\), \(q=\alpha+\beta>0\), \(\gamma>0\), and \(0<\eta<1/4\), so all these quantities are positive and finite.  Since \(n\ge12\) and \(m=\lfloor n/3\rfloor\),
\[
 n/4\le m\le n/3.
\tag{2}
\]
Because \(s=q/2\), the low-smoothness condition in \(\mathrm{def{:}phase\text{-}rate}\) is
\[
 q<{d\over2\{1+d/(2\gamma)\}}.
\tag{3}
\]
Moreover,
\[
 1+{d\over2\gamma}+{d\over2q}>2+{d\over\gamma}
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 q<{d\over2\{1+d/(2\gamma)\}},
\tag{4}
\]
with equality of the two powers on the boundary.  Therefore
\[
 r_{\mathrm{np}}=r_o\vee r_2.
\tag{5}
\]
Set
\[
 R=r_{\mathrm{np}}\vee r_{\mathrm{reg}}\vee r_{\mathrm{ho}}=r_{\mathrm{up}},
 \qquad t=1\wedge R.
\tag{6}
\]
Fix \(0<t_0<1\wedge r_0^\gamma\).  If \(t<t_0\), then \(t=R\) and
\[
 t\ge r_o,\quad t\ge r_2,
 \quad t\ge r_{\mathrm{reg}},\quad t\ge r_{\mathrm{ho}}.
\tag{7}
\]

For any admissible \((h,k)\), Definitions \(\mathrm{def{:}bias\text{-}envelope}\), \(\mathrm{def{:}sampling\text{-}envelope}\), and \(\mathrm{def{:}privacy\text{-}envelope}\) give, with
\[
 a=M^{-1/2},\qquad b={\sqrt{k}\over M},
\]
the bounds
\[
 B(h,k)\le C\{h^\gamma+\ell^q\},
\tag{8}
\]
\[
 S(h,k,\eta)=C_S\left\{
 \sqrt{x(a^2+b^2)}+xa^2+x^{3/2}ab+x^2b^2
 \right\},
\tag{9}
\]
and, using (2) and the definition of \(N_{\mathrm{priv}}\),
\[
 G(h,k,\eta,\epsilon_n,\delta_n)
 \le C N_{\mathrm{priv}}^{-1}\{h^{-d}+kh^{-2d}\}
 =C N_{\mathrm{priv}}^{-1}\{h^{-d}+h^{-d}\ell^{-d}\}.
\tag{10}
\]
In (8), \(h^\gamma\ell^\alpha\le h^\gamma\) because \(0<\ell\le h\le r_0\le1/4\) and \(\alpha>0\).  No rank inequality is used in (8)--(10).

Suppose first that \(q<\gamma\) and \(t<t_0\).  Choose
\[
 h=t^{1/\gamma},\qquad \ell_0=t^{1/q},
 \qquad K=(h/\ell_0)^d,\quad
 k=\max\{k_{\mathrm{poly}},\lceil K\rceil\}.
\tag{11}
\]
Since \(0<t<1\) and \(q<\gamma\), \(K\ge1\).  Therefore
\[
 K\le k\le \max\{2,k_{\mathrm{poly}}\}K,
 \qquad
 \max\{2,k_{\mathrm{poly}}\}^{-1/d}\ell_0
 \le\ell\le\ell_0.
\tag{12}
\]
The cutoff \(k\ge k_{\mathrm{poly}}\) is automatic, and the multipliers in (12) are fixed.  Equations (8), (11)--(12) give \(B(h,k)\le Ct\).  By (2), (7), and (1),
\[
 a=m^{-1/2}t^{-d/(2\gamma)}\le2t,
\tag{13}
\]
and
\[
 b\le C m^{-1}t^{-d/(2\gamma)-d/(2q)}\le Ct.
\tag{14}
\]
Indeed, the last inequalities in (13)--(14) are respectively equivalent to \(t\ge r_o\) and \(t\ge r_2\).  Substitution into (9), using \(t\le1\), gives \(S(h,k,\eta)\le Ct\).

On this branch \(\bar q=q\), so
\[
 r_{\mathrm{reg}}=N_{\mathrm{priv}}^{-1/(1+d/\gamma)},
 \qquad
 r_{\mathrm{ho}}=N_{\mathrm{priv}}^{-1/(1+d/\gamma+d/q)}.
\tag{15}
\]
The last two inequalities in (7) are equivalent to
\[
 N_{\mathrm{priv}}^{-1}t^{-d/\gamma}\le t,
 \qquad
 N_{\mathrm{priv}}^{-1}t^{-d/\gamma-d/q}\le t.
\tag{16}
\]
Equations (10)--(12) and (16) imply \(G(h,k,\eta,\epsilon_n,\delta_n)\le Ct\).  Hence
\[
 B(h,k)+S(h,k,\eta)+G(h,k,\eta,\epsilon_n,\delta_n)\le Ct.
\tag{17}
\]
This remains true when \(k>M\), because no envelope imposes an upper rank cap.

Now suppose \(q\ge\gamma\) and \(t<t_0\).  Choose
\[
 h=t^{1/\gamma},\qquad k=k_{\mathrm{poly}},
 \qquad \ell=h k_{\mathrm{poly}}^{-1/d}.
\tag{18}
\]
The integer \(k_{\mathrm{poly}}=(R_*+1)^d\) depends only on fixed smoothness and dimension parameters.  Thus \(\ell\) is comparable to \(h\), and \(q\ge\gamma\), \(h<1\), and \(\alpha>0\) give \(B(h,k_{\mathrm{poly}})\le Ct\).  Equation (13) remains valid, while
\[
 b={\sqrt{k_{\mathrm{poly}}}\over M}
 =\sqrt{k_{\mathrm{poly}}}\,a^2\le Ct^2.
\]
Equation (9) therefore yields \(S(h,k_{\mathrm{poly}},\eta)\le Ct\).  Here \(\bar q=\gamma\), and
\[
 r_{\mathrm{ho}}=N_{\mathrm{priv}}^{-1/(1+2d/\gamma)}.
\tag{19}
\]
The inequality \(t\ge r_{\mathrm{ho}}\) is equivalent to
\[
 N_{\mathrm{priv}}^{-1}t^{-2d/\gamma}\le t.
\tag{20}
\]
The two privacy terms in (10), evaluated at (18), are bounded by a fixed multiple of the left-hand side of (20), because \(h<1\) and \(k_{\mathrm{poly}}\) is fixed.  Thus (17) holds on this branch as well.  Equations (15)--(16) give the \(q\)-branch for \(q<\gamma\), while (19)--(20) give \(N_{\mathrm{priv}}^{-\gamma/(\gamma+2d)}\) for \(q\ge\gamma\).

We verify feasibility and existence.  In both branches \(h=t^{1/\gamma}<r_0\).  Equations (2), (7), and the definition of \(r_o\) imply
\[
 mh^d=mt^{d/\gamma}
 \ge{1\over4}n^{2\gamma/(2\gamma+d)}\longrightarrow\infty.
\tag{21}
\]
Thus the comparison pair is feasible for all sufficiently large \(n\).  For such \(n\), the feasible bandwidths form the nonempty compact interval
\[
 I_n=[\{C_S^2x/m\}^{1/d},r_0].
\]
Let \(F_n(h,k)=B(h,k)+S(h,k,\eta)+G(h,k,\eta,\epsilon_n,\delta_n)\).  The pair \((r_0,k_{\mathrm{poly}})\) is feasible, so \(V_n=F_n(r_0,k_{\mathrm{poly}})<\infty\).  The last term of the sampling envelope and \(h\le r_0\) imply
\[
 F_n(h,k)\ge {C_Sx^2\over m^2r_0^{2d}}k=:c_nk,
 \qquad c_n>0.
\tag{22}
\]
Consequently no integer \(k>V_n/c_n\) can minimize \(F_n\).  For each of the finitely many remaining integers \(k\ge k_{\mathrm{poly}}\), continuity in \(h\in I_n\) gives a minimizer.  Minimizing over this finite collection, with deterministic lexicographic tie-breaking, constructs the asserted \((\widehat h,\widehat k)\).

When \(t<t_0\), comparison with (11) or (18) and (17) gives \(F_n(\widehat h,\widehat k)\le Ct\).  Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}private\text{-}confidence\text{-}interval}\) clips the center into \([-1,1]\), and every envelope is nonnegative.  Hence the interval is nonempty on every transcript and
\[
 \operatorname{length}\{C_n(\widehat h,\widehat k)\}
 \le2F_n(\widehat h,\widehat k)\wedge2.
\tag{23}
\]
Thus its length is at most \(2Ct\) if \(t<t_0\).  If \(t\ge t_0\), (23) gives length at most \(2\le(2/t_0)t\).  These bounds are transcript-wise and uniform over \(Q\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{att}}\) and over the deterministic pilot dimensions.  Taking expectations and then the supremum over \(Q\), and using (6), proves the stated bound with \(t=1\wedge r_{\mathrm{up}}\).  The proof uses the fixed lower cutoff only to guarantee polynomial reproduction and never imposes an upper relation between \(k\) and \(mh^d\); it makes no full-class frontier claim.
